package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects multiple Android versions via APK infection)
package_info.why_malicious: CopyCat is a large-scale Android malware campaign that infected millions of devices, performing privilege escalation, ad fraud, and generating illicit revenue for its operators. The malware hijacks device functionality, installs additional payloads, and exfiltrates sensitive data, violating user trust and device security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for root access, installs a malicious payload as a system app, and escalates privileges, enabling persistent control over the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installing a new APK as a system app and modifying system directories is highly suspicious and indicative of privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps do not attempt to gain root access or install themselves as system apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management tools in enterprise environments may install system apps with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code generates fraudulent ad requests and simulates ad clicks, sending network traffic to ad servers to generate illicit revenue.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated ad click generation is a classic sign of ad fraud malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not simulate ad clicks or generate fake ad traffic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated testing frameworks may simulate ad clicks in controlled environments.
key_indicators: Automated HTTP requests to ad networks
No user interaction required for ad clicks

execution_context.file_location: malicious APK data exfiltration module (e.g., DataStealer.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive user data (contacts, device info) and exfiltrates it to a remote command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating user data to an external server is a hallmark of spyware and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not send sensitive user data to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup apps may upload data to trusted cloud services with user consent.
key_indicators: Collection of sensitive data without user consent
Network exfiltration to hardcoded C2 domains
Use of permissions not justified by app functionality

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious APK (CopyCat) on Android device.
Malware attempts to gain root access and installs itself as a system app for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent control and further malicious actions

attack_chain.action: Malware launches background services to perform ad fraud by simulating ad clicks and generating revenue.
Malware collects sensitive user data and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled servers.

behavioral_signatures: APK attempts to gain root access and install itself as a system app
Background services generating automated ad network traffic
Unauthorized collection and exfiltration of contacts, device info, or SMS
file_indicators: Presence of background services not declared in legitimate app manifest
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known CopyCat C2 domains
Unusual ad network traffic patterns from non-advertising apps
Data exfiltration to hardcoded IPs or domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for APKs requesting root access or attempting to write to /system/app, analyze network traffic for automated ad requests and data exfiltration, and flag apps that collect and transmit sensitive data without clear user consent. Use mobile security solutions to detect known CopyCat signatures and behaviors.
